abstract: Dr. Calvert discusses abnormal uterine bleeding, focusing on chronic anovulation from PCOS and insulin resistance. The lecture covers diagnostic criteria for PCOS (2 of 3: irregular menses, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound, elevated free testosterone), the pathophysiology of the menstrual cycle and hormonal feedback, and the strong association between PCOS and insulin resistance (20-80% of women). Management strategies include progesterone withdrawal to prevent endometrial cancer, birth control pills to increase SHBG and reduce free testosterone, spironolactone for hirsutism, and metformin for insulin resistance to restore ovulation. The talk emphasizes practical diagnostic and treatment approaches for family physicians.
key_points: Abnormal uterine bleeding is categorized as organic (pathologic) or functional (including chronic anovulation from PCOS and insulin resistance).
PCOS diagnosis requires 2 of 3: irregular menstrual periods, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound (specific request for follicle count <1 cm), and elevated free or total testosterone.
In the normal cycle, low estrogen triggers FSH, which converts androgen to estrogen; a rapid estrogen rise causes LH surge and ovulation; progesterone then stops endometrial proliferation.
In PCOS, there is a block in androgen-to-estrogen conversion, leading to low FSH, no LH surge, and chronic anovulation with high androgens.
Androgens decrease sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), magnifying free testosterone and causing hirsutism.
Insulin resistance is present in 20-80% of PCOS patients; testing fasting glucose/insulin ratio (normal >5) helps stratify severity and guides treatment.
Women with PCOS and amenorrhea must have uterine evacuation (withdrawal bleed) at least 2-3 times per year to prevent endometrial cancer.
Birth control pills provide 3-5 times normal estrogen levels, increasing SHBG and lowering free testosterone to slow hirsutism progression.
Metformin treatment for insulin resistance can normalize insulin, lower testosterone, and restore ovulation within 2-3 months.
Spironolactone prevents conversion of vellus hairs to terminal hairs but cannot reverse existing terminal hairs (require laser or electrolysis).
